verdict: Paylocity: Choose Paylocity when US mid-market payroll+HR with a modern employee app is the job and you will take a custom quote — not when you need Gusto’s published prices or Workday-class HCM. Scores use the HR editorial methodology from first-party research as of 2026-08-17 — not hands-on product testing.
bestFor: US mid-market companies (roughly 100–1,000 employees) that want payroll+HR in one modern platform
Teams comparing Paylocity vs ADP Workforce Now vs Paycor
Orgs that may add finance/IT and Ignite AI later
notIdealFor: Tiny teams that want Gusto’s published $49+$6 floor
Complex hourly WFM as the primary job (UKG Pro)
tradeoffs: Published free tiers vs paid depth for ATS, WFM, time, or training jobs
Hub / multi-module pricing complexity vs single-product floors
Mobile/frontline readiness vs desk-bound admin depth
Opaque contact-sales pricing vs transparent published seats
recommendation: Choose Paylocity when US mid-market payroll+HR with a modern employee app is the job and you will take a custom quote — not when you need Gusto’s published prices or Workday-class HCM. Compare Gusto for published SMB payroll, ADP Workforce Now for compliance-brand payroll, Paycor for a similar mid-market HCM, and Rippling if HR+IT unification is the job.

overallScoreRationale: Weighted average of the nine HR editorial criteria using the category weights (hiring/workforce fit 15, workflow depth 14, ease of use 12, integrations 12, value 12, mobile/frontline 10, scalability 9, analytics 8, AI 8), rounded to 1 decimal. Products are scored inside their job cluster — ATS, core HRIS, payroll/benefits, people-platform, enterprise HCM, frontline WFM, time & attendance, SOP training, and LMS peers are not forced into one undifferentiated ranking. Not a hands-on lab score, and affiliate economics are excluded.
